transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we approach the production policy review on August 25 for the public API rate-limit project, I want to make sure we're all aligned on the process. I'll be making the final decision on the policy that gets communicated to customers, but before I do, I need each of your teams — backend engineering, customer success, security, and support operations — to report your release-impacting findings. To give you context on the current draft: it allows 100 requests per minute for ordinary API keys, applies the same limit to authentication endpoints, and does not specify a staffed launch window. Please share any concerns or findings you have so I can record the final policy.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share a release-impacting finding from backend engineering. While testing an unrelated bulk-import client yesterday, I measured legitimate synchronization bursts of 145 requests in a minute. Backend's load replay confirms the policy needs an ordinary API-key limit of exactly 150 requests per minute with a 60-second burst window. The current draft's 100 requests per minute would be too low and could disrupt legitimate customer synchronization workflows. I haven't updated the policy draft yet because the client test was owned by another team, but this finding directly impacts the production policy decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from customer success. I confirmed with Acme's account team this morning that Acme's contract requires 14 calendar days' notice before enforcing a new API limit on Acme traffic. A notice sent on September 1 would permit enforcement on exactly September 15. I haven't entered this clause in the product launch ticket yet because legal confirmation arrived after the weekly review, but this contractual notice requirement directly impacts the policy launch timeline and needs to be factored into the final policy decision.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a release-impacting finding from security. During a credential-abuse investigation this afternoon, I measured automated login attempts against the authentication endpoints and confirmed that those endpoints require a separate limit of exactly 30 requests per minute per API key. The current draft applies the same 100 requests per minute limit to authentication endpoints, which would be far too permissive and would not adequately protect against credential-abuse attacks. This finding is not yet in the security tracker because the investigation is still being closed, but it directly impacts the production policy decision and the authentication endpoint limit needs to be set to 30 requests per minute per API key.
